idiom_name: mediating lookup service with a name-to-location binding table plus caching and invalidation policy
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a Name type (flat or compound) and a Lookup Service that maps names to resource handles or locations, plus a Registrar API so providers publish and withdraw bindings. Clients resolve by name at the point of use and treat the result as a binding with a lifetime; decide explicitly how bindings stay fresh (TTL, lease renewal, change notification) and how resolution failures are reported ('not found' versus 'service unavailable'). Do not let clients keep private fallback locations: either the binding lives in the lookup service or the dependency is injected. Where the platform already offers a naming facility (DNS, a container, a provider registry, the module system), wrap it behind this interface instead of writing a new registry.
code_sketch:
register(name, location)              # provider side, with lease/renewal
location = resolve(name)              # client side, at the point of use
if location is None: fail(name)       # 'not found' != 'lookup unavailable'
use(location)                         # result is a binding, not a constant
pitfalls: Keeping a resolved handle forever instead of re-resolving under a TTL or lease policy (stale binding).
Caching without an invalidation rule: the cache outlives the resource it points at.
Treating an unresolvable name as a fatal, unrecoverable error, or assuming the lookup service is always available.
Resolving synchronously on every use of a frequently-accessed resource: amortise with a client-side cache rather than hitting the lookup service on each call.
Lookup storms: many clients simultaneously re-resolving the same expired entry after a TTL expires - mitigate with jittered TTLs or a distributed cache that refreshes proactively before expiry.
Namespace collisions: two independent registrars binding the same flat name without a shared namespace prefix, silently overwriting each other's bindings.

Wrong move: treat a successful, health-filtered lookup as proof the resource is usable -> health data can race with failure and a resolved endpoint can still reject or time out -> instead apply bounded connect/call timeouts, retry only transient failures with backoff, and use circuit breaking after resolution.

Wrong move: expose an ambient service locator as the lookup API for every dependency -> hidden preconditions fail at runtime and the dependency graph disappears from static interfaces -> instead inject a narrowly typed lookup client at the composition boundary and keep resolved resources explicit.
